title: Batcher Loom: workload drift-aware profiling and canary apply orchestrator
creator: Ava Mitchell
description: Create 'Batcher Loom', a continuous recommendation engine that profiles live workload signatures, detects drift, synthesizes batching and KV-cache parameters, and orchestrates a staged canary apply with automatic rollback heuristics. The engine must produce explainable recommendations, attach confidence bands, and integrate with Console rollouts and the safe-apply controller. This ticket covers profiler design, heuristic rule-set, scoring model, canary orchestration flow, rollback triggers, and observability hooks.
goal: Reduce per-token inference cost by 12-20% for eligible workloads while keeping P95 latency regression <5% and eliminating high-risk blind applies. Provide safe automated suggestions deployable by Console's rollout system with one-click canary/apply/rollback.
success_metrics: median unit-cost reduction for targeted services >= 12% within 30 days
P95 latency change across canary cohorts <= +5%
false-positive rollback rate < 3% over first 1k applies
eng ops manual intervention rate during canaries < 10%
acceptance_criteria: Profiler ingests per-request metadata (seq_len, model_variant, route, customer_tier) and outputs a rolling 7-day signature distribution
Recommendation API returns parameter set {microbatch_size, max_batch_delay_ms, kv_cache_ttl, coalescing_window_ms} with confidence score and delta cost/latency estimate
Canary orchestrator integrates with Console rollouts: create canary slice, apply config to slice, monitor SLOs, auto-promote or rollback based on heuristics
Rollback triggers include: SLO breach (P95 latency > baseline + 5%), error-rate spike (>2x baseline), quality regressions flagged by eval hooks
Telemetry panorama in Console shows before/after cost breakdown, traffic split, and a one-click revert
End-to-end e2e test and a phased shadow-apply run scheduled on 50 low-risk customers
notes: 2026-03-01: Kickoff with PM and Observability. Agreed to use existing trace and token telemetry as primary signals.

2026-03-03: Prototype profiler built — windowed histograms for seq_len, response-time quantiles, and coalescing opportunities. Initial results show high batching opportunity on chat completion routes.
2026-03-05: Design decision: hybrid heuristic+statistical scoring vs ML model. Chose hybrid for interpretability; ML reserved for later iterations if signal complexity grows.
2026-03-06: Security review flagged requirement to not expose customer identifiers in recommendation payloads. Added aggregation and hashing step.
2026-03-08: Canary plan drafted: 0.5% traffic -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% increments with 24h observation windows and staged rollback backoffs.
2026-03-09: UX sync — Console team will surface recommendation rationale and per-parameter confidence bands; added acceptance criteria for explainability texts.
2026-03-10: Implementation started: backend API endpoints + telemetry pipeline schema changes. Diego to own rollout controller integration PR. Ref PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infra/pull/4321
